entries.reason: iOS 6 rounds all four corners of a layer together, so a selection short of all four is a mask of the layer laid over the two corners it clips
entries.effect: a layer that clips to its bounds with a corner radius, and is masked to fewer than all four corners, gets a CAShapeLayer mask of a rect rounded on exactly the selected corners (UIBezierPath's own byRoundingCorners:cornerRadii:, since CACornerMask and UIRectCorner share the same four bit positions), kept in step with its bounds, radius and mask; a layer masked to all four corners (the default) or one that does not clip, or already has a mask of its own, is untouched. Not coordinated with cornerCurve: both features hold layer.mask on the same terms, so whichever of setCornerCurve: or setMaskedCorners: was called more recently keeps it, and the other stays inert until set again - the rare combination of both is not specially handled
